chapter: Jess Stacy, Goodman and New York characters
title: Meeting the boy Benny Goodman at Hull House
summary: Hodes recalls Goodman as a boy brought to play with him at Hull House. Hodes was not impressed.

story.theme_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the leader and his bands
story.community_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the perfectionist bandleader

blocks.x: And everybody -- the King was here, the whole place they're running to his table. I didn't run to his table, because I remember him as a kid. See, we were kids at Hull House, and his bandmaster brought him in to where I was playing for the dancers. And he asked me if I minded if the kid played with me. And I looked at this kid, with a head that seemed so outsized and even though the head was outsized, the ego was outsized, too. And he had such an assurance, and just a tilt of the nose, almost.
About how old was he then?
Oh, if I was 12, he was nine. I don't know. How much difference, but I was just -- if I was a teenager, he had to be 13. Just very -- so whatever he was, in relationship to me. But he could play.

But I wasn't that impressed, because -- I says, yeah, you play nice. I didn't hear no great ideas. I've never heard anything out of him that I want to go down the street and whistle, as I have with Louis Armstrong. I have with Bix, I have with any number of people. I never heard a thing out of him that I -- I've even heard with Tatum, that little introduction or little something going on that I want to sing when I get out. I never heard that with Benny.
But I heard that he knew his instrument, but that didn't impress me that much. I wasn't impressed with that nonsense. And that's the time we met. So when I saw him
